post.title: Your employer goes bankrupt. What happens to your pension?
post.ig:
Your employer goes broke. Your pension has a $7,790 ceiling.

The PBGC insures most private pensions: about 30 million people, $6.4B+ paid in FY2025.
The 2026 single-employer cap: $7,789.77 a month at age 65. Most retirees fall under it and are paid in full.
Your 401(k) is held in trust, separate from company assets.

Sources: PBGC FY2025 Annual Report, PBGC 2026 guarantee tables, US Dept. of Labor.
News and education, not financial advice.

If a private employer with a pension goes bankrupt, the federal PBGC steps in. It protects about 30 million people and paid over $6.4 billion in FY2025. For plans ending in 2026, the guarantee caps at $7,789.77 a month at age 65; most retirees are under the cap and paid in full. 401(k)s are held in trust, separate from company assets. Sources: PBGC, US Dept. of Labor.
